prize_parts.citation: For methods to estimate demand and market equilibrium in differentiated-product industries from market-level data, which made structural empirical industrial organisation practical.

statement.case_for: The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes framework solved a concrete problem. It estimates substitution patterns with random coefficients while treating price endogeneity in market-level data. It has since become routine in merger review, antitrust, regulation, trade and other fields, and it is taught as standard method. It has had three decades of replication and methodological refinement, including work on instruments, computation and inference. So the maturity concern that applies to younger candidates does not apply here. The attribution is also tighter than in several higher-profile candidates. The BLP core is a short, identifiable chain of papers (Berry 1994; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes 1995), and Pakes has a separate, well-defined line on dynamic industry models. A three-person prize therefore follows a real intellectual unit and does not require arbitrary cuts, unlike B015 with its eight credited names or B002 with its large team. Under common criteria of originality, durability and breadth of use, I think the case holds in any field.
statement.case_against: My opening ranking put B022 first, and no one else has put it in first place. Only Tommy Andersson also ranked it. Low support does not weaken the science, but it does mean this configuration cannot reach six votes without a substantial change in other members' views. Substantively, the identification of the BLP approach rests on strong assumptions about instruments and functional form. Bresnahan's earlier work on identifying market power and demand in empirical IO is a real precursor, and its omission is a genuine attribution question. The dynamic-industry strand in the credited list (Ericson-Pakes, Benkard, Levin) is only loosely tied to the BLP trio. Finally, I work in this field, so my familiarity could inflate my assessment.

responses.point: He ranked the same BLP trio sixth. He noted that Bresnahan's contributions could be argued as equally central, and that the dynamic-industry part is less closely tied to the BLP trio.
responses.response: I agree that the dynamic-games strand is linked to Pakes alone and does not belong to the demand-estimation core. That is why my citation covers only demand and market equilibrium in differentiated-product industries. I only partly agree on Bresnahan. His identification work on market power and demand is an important precursor and a fair reason to hesitate. But the contribution I would credit is the estimable framework that handles heterogeneous consumers, endogenous prices and market-level data together, and that is what Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes supplied. I accept that this is a judgement and that a committee could reasonably prefer a broader empirical-IO prize.

responses.point: He ranked Melitz and Helpman second under B033. He treated Redding as more recent and derivative, and he flagged that Krugman's 2008 prize may reduce the appetite for another trade award.
responses.response: I share his view that Redding's contribution is quantitative and spatial and should not sit in the core credit, and my own B033 proposal is also the Helpman-Melitz pair. I am less persuaded that the 2008 prize is a strong obstacle. Melitz (2003) introduced selection into exporting and reallocation as a source of gains from trade, which is different from the scale-and-variety logic of new trade theory. My reservation is attribution, not overlap. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made closely related contributions and are not credited on B033. For that reason I would keep B033 as an alternative and not as my first choice.

responses.point: He ranked B002 first for its population-scale administrative data and credible quasi-experimental designs on neighbourhood effects. He noted that the three-name cap forces a choice among Chetty, Hendren, Friedman and Katz, and that some long-run causal claims are still being tested.
responses.response: I take the scientific case seriously, and it is why I include B002 as an alternative and not as a mere filler. The new data and the design-based evidence on place effects are a real advance. I still have two reservations that his arguments do not remove. One is maturity, because most of the core results are under a decade old and the causal interpretation of exposure effects is still contested. The other is credit within a large collaborative programme. His point that Katz is left off to respect the cap shows how unclean that attribution is. These are reasons for caution, not for rejection. If the Committee decides that replication so far is sufficient, I would not oppose the Chetty-Hendren-Friedman trio.

responses.point: He ranked B015 first and called nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and policy rules the working core of modern monetary policy analysis, with Calvo, Taylor and Woodford as a defensible trio.
responses.response: I agree that the framework is foundational and highly influential in policy practice, and I would pick the same three names. I rank it lower because my own work on price adjustment, including firm surveys and retail price data, shows that time-dependent Calvo pricing fits micro price data only partly. Asymmetric and state-dependent adjustment matter, so the empirical foundations are less settled than the policy influence suggests. Also, as he says, the cut among at least five other strong contributors is arbitrary. That is a real attribution cost, and it applies to few other candidates.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers a narrow BLP prize or a broader empirical-IO prize that would include Bresnahan, and possibly Reiss, Benkard and Levin.
How much weight identification assumptions (instruments, functional form) should carry in judging a methodological contribution.

Whether B002 has enough replication and long-run confirmation to outweigh its recency and its diffuse team credit, and whether B033 can be credited cleanly given the missing Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum strand.
How far my own familiarity with industrial organisation shapes my assessment of B022 relative to fields I know less well.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent for the credited candidates in the supplied profile. I have no listed co-authorship with any credited name on the shortlist. I co-authored with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026), which does not concern any shortlisted candidate. My field, industrial organisation, is close to B022, so I note it for weighting. My spouse's public political role is a public fact and, as far as the profile shows, has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate.
